facts.text: Gibson was an early Arkansas settlement founded after the territorial capital moved to Little Rock in 1821, attracting farmers and land grant holders.
The Southwest Trail, a military road from El Paso to North Little Rock, cut through Gibson, making it a key stop for pioneers heading to Texas.
Gibson’s silver deposits once gave North Little Rock the nickname Argenta, derived from the Latin word for silver.
In the 1840s, blacksmith Benjamin Kellogg claimed to find lead ore while tunneling crayfish near what is now Kellogg Creek, sparking early mining.
Three mine shafts in Gibson revealed veins of silver, copper, lead, and zinc, but most miners abandoned the area in 1849 for California’s gold rush.
A 1925 reopening of Gibson’s mines produced 3,118 troy ounces of silver, worth $2,164 at the time, showing a brief revival.
